candidates: When implementing a function like `replaceIconSubstring` that must make async calls for each regex match, use a two-pass approach: (1) call `text.replace(regex, ...)` to collect a `Promise[]` of all async substitutions without modifying the string, (2) resolve them with `await Promise.all(...)`, then (3) call `text.replace(regex, () => resolved.shift())` on the **original text** to apply results. Running the second pass on the original text is critical — applying it to already-substituted output risks re-matching `fa:xxx` patterns that appear inside inserted SVG strings.

When a change alters externally-visible output (e.g., CSS class names on generated HTML elements, API return format), verify whether it is a breaking change and, if so, mark the changeset as `major` or explicitly describe the breaking behavior in the changeset message and PR description so downstream users know to update dependent code.

Do not include changes to `pnpm-lock.yaml` unless the PR actually adds, removes, or upgrades package dependencies. Spurious lockfile diffs significantly increase merge-conflict risk for other open PRs and should be reverted before review.

When building HTML strings that include attribute values derived from user input, apply `sanitizeText` (or an equivalent escaper) and verify the result cannot contain the quote character used to delimit the attribute. A single-quote-delimited attribute that passes through a general sanitizer may still be an XSS vector if the sanitizer does not strip or escape single quotes.

When documenting a feature that works only with certain diagram types or accepts only a specific set of values (e.g., FontAwesome icon prefixes `fa`, `fab`, `fas`, `far`, `fal`, `fad`), explicitly state which diagram types are supported and list all accepted values in the documentation. Do not leave readers to infer scope or valid inputs from examples alone.

In documentation files under `src/docs/`, always write `v<MERMAID_RELEASE_VERSION>` (not a hardcoded semver string) when marking the version in which a feature was introduced. The release tooling replaces this token with the actual version at publish time.

Changeset messages must be specific: name the affected diagram type(s) and describe the concrete behavioral change (e.g., 'FontAwesome icons can now be embedded as SVGs in flowcharts via `mermaid.registerIconPacks`') rather than making a general statement that could mislead users about the scope of the change.

In Cypress HTML fixtures (e.g., `cypress/platform/e2e.html`), avoid top-level `svg { ... }` rules that inadvertently style nested SVGs such as inline icon SVGs or sub-diagram SVGs. Scope decorative or debug styles to the root Mermaid SVG only, for example using `svg:not(svg svg)` or `div.mermaid svg:first-of-type`.

Do not load fonts, icon packs, or other test resources from remote CDN URLs in Cypress E2E tests. Use locally-installed package copies (as the docs site does) to prevent snapshot flakiness caused by network latency, CDN unavailability, or silent resource changes.

In `cypress/platform/viewer.js` and similar Cypress test harnesses, explicitly await all web-font loads with `await Promise.all(Array.from(document.fonts, (font) => font.load()))` before triggering diagram rendering. Failing to do so causes layout-dependent snapshot tests to flake when fonts haven't finished downloading.

In Cypress viewer helper functions (e.g., `loadFontAwesomeCSS`), do not silently catch and swallow resource-load errors. Allow the returned Promise to reject on failure so that Cypress surfaces a clear, actionable error rather than failing later with a confusing visual diff.

When changes to shared Cypress infrastructure (e.g., `cypress/platform/viewer.js`) alter the rendering environment — such as adding font loading, changing viewport, or modifying layout — audit all dependent spec files for hard-coded dimension or size assertions (e.g., `within(N * 0.95, N * 1.05)` checks) and update them to reflect the new rendering baseline.

Do not use generic phrases such as 'here', 'click here', or 'learn more' as hyperlink text in documentation. Per W3C guidelines, link text should describe the destination or purpose of the link (e.g., `["Registering icon packs" instructions](../config/icons.md)` rather than `[here](../config/icons.md)`).

When test or source files embed third-party assets such as FontAwesome SVG path data, add an inline comment (or `@license` / `@copyright` JSDoc tags) that identifies the license (e.g., CC-BY-4.0), copyright holder, and source URL. Omitting attribution may expose the project to license-compliance or DMCA issues.

CSS rules that apply to icons or other shared UI elements across multiple diagram types must be defined once in `src/diagrams/globalStyles.ts` (exported as `getIconStyles()` or a similar helper) and imported into each diagram's `styles.ts`/`styles.js`. Do not duplicate the same CSS block inline across individual diagram style modules.
